children: turns 30 today, having been founded on September 25, 1996. The company was started when 24-year-old former University of Maryland football special teams captain named Kevin Plank started selling moisture-wicking T-shirts out of his grandmother's basement in Washington, D.C.

To launch the business, Plank spent his time traveling along the East Coast with nothing but apparel in his car's trunk of his car before landing his first team deal at the end of 1996 with a $17K sales The company relocated to Baltimore and grew from a scrappy startup into one of the biggest names in performance sportswear.

went public in 2005 with an IPO, and by 2010 the company had crossed $1B in annual revenue. Its "Protect This House" campaign and gear built around moisture-wicking compression fabric helped it carve out a distinct niche against giants like Nike
, and partnerships with athletes such as Stephen Curry and Tom Brady cemented its cultural relevance through the 2010s, pushing revenue past $5B a year.

However, starting around 2016, growth stalled and the stock cratered amid inventory gluts, discounting, and intensifying competition. Plank stepped down from his role as CEO, and the company later disclosed it was under federal investigation to determine whether the brand altered its recorded revenue to bolster its healthy appearance. A string of subsequent CEOs struggled to reverse the slide, layoffs and restructurings became routine, and the company posted more annual net losses.

is leaning once again on its founder to steer the next chapter. Plank returned to the CEO position in March 2024 after two external leaders failed to bring meaningful improvements. His turnaround plan centers on cutting SKUs by roughly a quarter, pulling back on discounting, and repositioning the brand as more premium, with its sports focus reset following the end of its long-running partnership with Steph Curry. Notably, Plank and his team are targeting a return to growth by FY28, with North America expected to stabilize first and international markets already showing modest gains as the brand begins its fourth decade.

title: Under Armour at 30: A legacy of innovation, setbacks, and reinvention
